title: MidPC LoRA: Intermediate SVD Slices for Continual Learning with Low-Rank Adaptation

contributions.purpose: Improve the stability-plasticity trade-off of LoRA in continual learning by choosing a better spectral region for adapter initialization.
contributions.mechanism: MidPC (Middle Principal Components) initializes LoRA adapters from intermediate singular components of the pretrained weight SVD, rather than top (PiSSA) or bottom (MiLoRA) components, requiring no architectural changes or replay buffers.
contributions.evaluation: On the FOREVER Standard CL benchmark with Qwen3-0.6B, MidPC achieves 84.8% overall performance and -1.7% backward transfer.
contributions.domain: Continual learning / parameter-efficient fine-tuning of LLMs
contributions.source_quote: First, we propose MidPC, a simple SVD-slice initialization strategy that selects intermediate singular components for LoRA adapters in continual learning.

contributions.purpose: Establish MidPC as the best-performing SVD-based initialization for reducing forgetting.
contributions.mechanism: Benchmarks MidPC against PiSSA and MiLoRA on forgetting/backward-transfer metrics.
contributions.evaluation: Reduces forgetting by 13.3 percentage points vs PiSSA (66.7%, -15.0%) and 3.3 percentage points vs MiLoRA (81.6%, -5.0%).
contributions.source_quote: Second, we demonstrate that MidPC achieves state-of-the-art performance among SVD-based methods, reducing forgetting by 13.3 percentage points compared to PiSSA and 3.3 percentage points compared to MiLoRA.

contributions.purpose: Explain why intermediate slices help and confirm the effect is genuinely spectral rather than an artifact of conditioning.
contributions.mechanism: Spectral analysis of subspace alignment and spectral imbalance, plus learning-rate-matching experiments that control for conditioning differences.
contributions.evaluation: MidPC maintains stable subspace alignment with moderate spectral imbalance; 91.9% of the advantage over MiLoRA is retained after controlling for conditioning.
contributions.source_quote: Third, we provide spectral analysis showing that MidPC maintains stable subspace alignment while achieving moderate spectral imbalance, and verify through learning rate matching that the improvement reflects a genuine spectral effect, with 91.9% of the advantage over MiLoRA retained after controlling for conditioning differences.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Recent work has explored SVD-based initialization strategies to address this: PiSSA (Meng et al., 2024) initializes adapters from top singular components for faster convergence, while MiLoRA (Wang et al., 2024) uses bottom components to preserve pretrained knowledge. Yet these approaches represent endpoint choices on the singular spectrum, leaving the intermediate region unexplored.
We propose MidPC (Middle Principal Components), which initializes LoRA adapters from the middle of the singular spectrum.
These findings motivate our investigation of intermediate spectral regions, which may offer a better balance between learning capacity and stability.

notes: Contributions stated as inline prose (threefold: First/Second/Third), not a bullet list.
